name: Chen Yilun
current_role: Founder & CEO, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Chen Yilun co-founded TARS in Feb 2025 with ex-Baidu IDG president Li Zhenyu and ex-Huawei 'Genius Youth' Ding Wenchao. He was previously CTO of autonomous driving and chief scientist of Huawei's automotive BU, then chief robotics scientist at Tsinghua AIR. TARS builds industrial general-purpose robots (AWE foundation model, DexHand) and raised a record ~$455M Pre-A in April 2026.
interesting_fact: TARS's 2026 Pre-A round of about $455M (3.1bn yuan) was described as the largest single financing round in China's embodied-intelligence sector.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his bachelor's and master's in electronic engineering at Tsinghua and a PhD in EE from the University of Michigan (2011), and before Huawei was chief machine-vision engineer at DJI.
notes: Company press contact is published on TARS's PR Newswire releases. Chen has argued embodied AI today resembles intelligent driving around 2019; good podcast angle (autonomy to robotics).

name: Victor Cardenas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Slash (San Francisco vertical-banking fintech)
profile: Venezuelan-born Thiel Fellow who dropped out of Stanford to co-found Slash with Kevin Bai. Slash began offering cards and banking to sneaker resellers, then pivoted to industry-specific ('vertical') banking for ad buyers, e-commerce, web3 and more; it raised a $100M Series C from Khosla and Ribbit at a $1.4B valuation.
interesting_fact: After the 2022 Kanye West/Adidas fallout hit the sneaker-resale market, Slash's revenue reportedly fell about 80% almost overnight, prompting the pivot to vertical banking; Cardenas later said over 1% of all Facebook ads were bought with a Slash card.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Caracas during the onset of hyperinflation, he built his first 'fintech' for his school cantina, which was forced to sell food without cash; at 19, as a Stanford sophomore, he co-founded Tabtab, an app for splitting subscriptions and rent.
notes: No published press email on slash.com (only support@slash.com, customer support). He says he reads mostly biographies (Napoleon, Hamilton, Juan Vicente Gomez) and is 'bullish on Venezuela' (Fintech Leaders interview).

name: Hamish McKenzie
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Writing Officer, Substack
profile: New Zealand-born writer who co-founded Substack in 2017 with Chris Best and Jairaj Sethi. Before that he was a PandoDaily tech reporter, worked at Kik, and was a lead writer at Tesla, which he wrote about in the 2018 book 'Insane Mode'. He is Substack's public voice on independent media; Substack raised a $100M Series C in 2025.
interesting_fact: He worked as a writer at Tesla and turned the experience into the 2018 book 'Insane Mode: How Elon Musk's Tesla Sparked an Electric Revolution to End the Age of Oil'.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Alexandra, Central Otago, and has wanted to be a writer since childhood; at about eight he wrote a series about 'crocodiles trapped in the toilet'.
notes: Very accessible; does many podcasts and talks. His own Substack is the most natural outreach channel. Reportedly writing a book, 'How to Save the Media'.
